record.paper_title: Finiteness and periodicity of beta expansions – number theoretical and dynamical open problems
record.original_question: For a Salem number beta, let d_beta(x) be the greedy beta-expansion digit sequence of x in [0,1). Is d_beta(x) eventually periodic for every x in Q(beta) ∩ [0,1)?

evidence.quote: If β is a Pisot number, then dβ(x) is eventually periodic for x ∈ Q(β) ∩ [0, 1).
Problem 4. (Salem Periodicity Problem 2) For Salem β, is dβ(x) eventually periodic for all x ∈ Q(β) ∩ [0, 1) ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let β > 1 be a real number. The greedy β-expansion of x ∈ [0,1) is the sequence d_β(x) = (a_1, a_2, a_3, …) of nonnegative integers a_i ∈ {0, 1, …, ⌈β⌉−1} defined by the iteration of the β-transformation T_β(y) = βy − ⌊βy⌋: set a_i = ⌊β T_β^{i−1}(x)⌋ for i ≥ 1, so that x = ∑_{i≥1} a_i β^{−i}. The sequence d_β(x) is said to be eventually periodic if there exist integers N ≥ 0 and p ≥ 1 such that a_{n+p} = a_n for every n > N.

A Salem number is a real algebraic integer β > 1 all of whose other Galois conjugates have modulus ≤ 1, with at least one conjugate of modulus exactly 1. Let Q(β) denote the field generated by β over the rationals.

Question: For every Salem number β, is the greedy β-expansion d_β(x) eventually periodic for every x ∈ Q(β) ∩ [0,1)?
artifact.status_search_result: The analogous statement for Pisot β is a theorem of Schmidt (1980), but the Salem case is widely regarded as open. It is known only in restricted situations (e.g., for Salem β of degree 4, by Boyd), and even the eventual periodicity of d_β(1) is conjectural for general Salem β, verified only in low degree with conflicting heuristics in higher degree.

status_evidence.title: On Periodic Expansions of Pisot Numbers and Salem Numbers (Schmidt 1980)
status_evidence.snippet: Shows that if β is Pisot, every x∈Q(β)∩[0,1) has eventually periodic β-expansion; the analogous question for Salem numbers is posed.
status_evidence.claim: The Pisot case is solved; the Salem case is raised as an open question.

status_evidence.title: Periodic representations in Salem bases (arXiv:1812.08228)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies periodicity properties of representations in Salem bases, indicating the periodicity question for Salem β remains open in general.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work still treats the Salem periodicity problem as unresolved.

status_evidence.title: On the beta expansion for Salem numbers of degree 6
status_evidence.snippet: Boyd proved eventual periodicity for degree 4 Salem β; conjectured for degree 6, but conjectured to fail for some degree 8 Salem numbers.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial low-degree results are known; full conjecture not established.
